subtitle: Land, Steel and the Drum of the Gajapati

panels.shot: epic wide-angle of terraced fields merging into a distant fortified hill, a lone Paika standing between plough and spear
panels.action: The Paika of Odisha stands at the edge of a green paddy, one hand on a wooden plough, the other resting on a gleaming spear, as a distant hill-fort rises over the misty horizon.

dialogue.text: In the age of the Gajapatis, the Paikas of Odisha tilled rent-free land in peace and marched as warriors in war — a kingdom’s strength rooted in the soil beneath their feet.

i18n.hi: गजपति के ज़माने में ओडिशा के पाइका शाँत दिनों में बे-मुज़रिया ज़मीन जोतते, और जंग में योद्धा बन चल पड़ते — उनकी ताकत पैरों के नीचे की मिट्टी से उठती थी।

panels.shot: low, atmospheric wide shot of coastal Odisha at dawn, showing villages, temple spires and a distant port, with a Gajapati banner fluttering
panels.action: At dawn, the Paika of Odisha looks out over a patchwork of paddy fields, village roofs and temple spires, while far away a Gajapati lion-banner snaps in the sea breeze near a busy coastal port.

dialogue.text: From Chilika’s mist to the ports of Kalinga’s coast, the Gajapatis ruled a land where village, temple and fort were bound together by men who were both farmers and fighters.

i18n.hi: चिलिका की धुंध से कलिंग तट के बंदरगाहों तक, गजपति उस धरती पर राज करते थे जहाँ गाँव, मंदिर और किला उन किसानों–सैनिकों से एक डोर में बँधे थे।

panels.shot: medium close-up of the Paika’s hands switching from plough-handle to spear-shaft, with cracked earth and young rice shoots underfoot
panels.action: The Paika of Odisha’s rough hands release the wooden plough and close firmly around a polished spear-shaft, young rice shoots and dry clods of earth visible beneath his feet.

dialogue.text: Their duty was written into the land itself: in return for plots light in tax or free of rent, the Paikas owed their bodies and skill-at-arms whenever the Gajapati called.

i18n.hi: उनकी ड्यूटी ज़मीन में ही लिखी थी: हलकी लगान या बे-मुज़रिया टुकड़ों के बदले, गजपति की पुकार पर पाइका अपना जिस्म और हथियार लगा देने को बँधे थे।

panels.shot: interior village courtyard, slightly high angle, showing a palm-leaf grant being read aloud as Paikas and elders listen
panels.action: In a village courtyard, the Paika of Odisha kneels among other armed farmers as an elder holds up a palm-leaf grant, the faint impression of a royal seal visible, while villagers listen in tense silence.

dialogue.text: Grants on palm leaf promised service land to lineages: if the men turned out with shield and spear when summoned, their fields would be theirs, generation after generation.

i18n.hi: ताड़पत्र पर लिखे दान बताते थे सेवा–ज़मीन के हक: बुलावे पर ढाल–भाला लेकर निकले तो खेत उनके, पीढ़ी दर पीढ़ी चले आते।

panels.shot: inside a village house, close shot of a weapons rack beside agricultural tools
panels.action: In the dim light of a mud-walled house, the Paika of Odisha stands before a rack where a khanda-like sword, spear and shield hang beside a sickle, plough yoke and rope basket.

dialogue.text: So, in Paika homes, sword and plough lived side by side. The same men who repaired bunds and raised seedlings drilled with bows, lances and the heavy Odia sword.

i18n.hi: इस तरह पाइका घरों में तलवार और हल साथ–साथ रहते। जो हाथ बाँध मरम्मत और पौधे रोपते, वही धनुष, भाला और भारी ओड़िया तलवार से रोज़ मशक करते।

panels.shot: dynamic training ground wide shot, showing Paikas practicing in formation near a village edge, a temple in the background
panels.action: Near the village boundary, the Paika of Odisha moves in rhythm with a line of men, shields up and spears thrusting in unison, while a small temple and peepal tree rise behind them.

dialogue.text: Sarala Das sang of war-bands and their drills: companies of foot and horse practising charges, shield-walls and arrow storms, their names and rhythms preserved in his Odia verses.

i18n.hi: सरला दास ने इन युद्ध–दल और उनकी कसरतें गाईं: पैदल और घुड़सवार टुकड़ियाँ, धावा, ढाल–दीवार और तीरों की बारिश साधती, जिनके नाम और ताल उनकी ओड़िया कविताओं में बस गए।

panels.shot: low, intense shot of a war drummer beating a great drum as Paikas look up from their fields
panels.action: A war drummer stands on a raised mound, striking a great leather drum, while in the middle ground the Paika of Odisha and other farmers straighten from their fields, faces turning toward the sound.

dialogue.text: When the kingdom needed them, it was not a written summons but the drum that spoke. War music rolled over the paddies, and tools fell from hands that reached for spears.

i18n.hi: जब राज्य को ज़रूरत पड़ती, तो लिखी चिट्ठी नहीं, ढोल बोलता था। युद्ध–नगाड़ा धान–खेतों पर गूंजता, औज़ार हाथ से छूटकर उसी हाथ में भाला थमा देता।

panels.shot: crowded mustering ground mid-wide, Paikas assembling under a lion banner, with coastal hills in the distance
panels.action: On a dusty field, the Paika of Odisha tightens a cloth around his waist as rows of armed men gather under a lion-emblazoned banner, the hazy outline of coastal hills beyond.

dialogue.text: Foreign eyes noticed this strength. Fernao Nunes, travelling in the south, wrote of the Gajapati’s armies as countless, fields emptying into ranks of disciplined men when the lion banner rose.

i18n.hi: बाहरवालों ने भी ये ताकत देखी। दक्षिण घूमता फर्नाव नुनेश लिख गया कि गजपति की फौजें अनगिनत हैं, शेर–झंडा उठते ही खेत खाली हो पंक्तियों में सधे सिपाही भर जाते हैं।

panels.shot: side-on medium shot of Paikas marching along an embankment, with ships and a port town visible below
panels.action: The Paika of Odisha marches in file along a raised embankment, his spear over his shoulder, as below them a busy port town hums with moored ships and warehouses.

dialogue.text: From inland forts to coastal ports, Paika contingents moved along ancient routes. Their bodies shielded the trade that flowed through Odisha’s harbours and the shrines that anchored its people.

i18n.hi: भीतर के किलों से समुद्री बंदरगाहों तक, पाइका दल पुराने रास्तों पर चलते रहे। उनके बदन ओडिशा के बाज़ारों और बंदरगाहों की राह ढँकते, और उन देवालयों को बचाते जो लोगों की जान से जुड़े थे।

panels.shot: stormy battlefield wide shot, Paika line braced with spears and shields as opposing forces loom in the haze
panels.action: Under a brooding sky, the Paika of Odisha stands in a bristling hedge of spears and round shields, facing a shadowy opposing host emerging from the dust-haze across the plain.

dialogue.text: On distant fields, the Paikas learned the hard cost of their land. Sarala Das described shields locking, drums pounding, elephants advancing while foot-soldiers like them held the line for king and village.

i18n.hi: दूर के मैदानों पर पाइका ने अपनी ज़मीन की असली कीमत जानी। सरला दास ने ढालों के जाम होने, नगाड़ों के गरजने, हाथियों के बढ़ने और ऐसे पैदलों को लिखा जो राजा और गाँव के लिए मोर्चा पकड़ खड़े रहे।

panels.shot: moody interior of a temple courtyard, Paikas gathered as priests bless their weapons
panels.action: In a temple courtyard lit by lamps, the Paika of Odisha bows as a priest sprinkles water over a row of laid-out swords and spears, other Paikas watching with solemn faces.

dialogue.text: Temples were not only places of worship; they were nodes of this military economy. Land endowed to shrines was worked by service groups, and Paikas stood among those who guarded and benefited from that order.

i18n.hi: मंदिर केवल पूजा के ठिकाने नहीं थे; वही इस सैन्य–इकोनॉमी के जोड़–बिंदु थे। देवता के नाम की ज़मीन सेवा–गिरोह जोतते, और पाइका भी उन रक्षकों की कतार में थे जो इस व्यवस्था के तौर–तरीके से जीते थे।

panels.shot: evening village scene, Paika returning, greeted by family at the edge of their fields
panels.action: At dusk, the Paika of Odisha trudges back along the bund, shield strapped to his back, as his family waits at the field’s edge, a child clutching his leg and an elder touching his shoulder.

dialogue.text: When campaigns ended, they came back not to barracks but to furrows and families. Their reward was not only pay, but the right to sow and harvest on land held by warrior service.

i18n.hi: मुहिम के बाद वे बैरकों में नहीं, फिर खेतों और परिवारों में लौटते। उनका इनाम सिर्फ़ तनख़्वाह नहीं, बल्कि उसी सेवा–ज़मीन पर बीज डालने और फ़सल काटने का हक था।

panels.shot: close-up of an elder Paika teaching a boy to read a palm-leaf, weapons faintly visible behind
panels.action: Inside a verandah, an elder Paika of Odisha guides a young boy’s finger along incised letters on a palm leaf, while in the blurred background a spear and sword lean against the wall.

dialogue.text: Over time, this duty hardened into identity. Lineages of Khandayats and Paikas saw themselves as hereditary defenders, their status tied to land grants and remembered campaigns.

i18n.hi: धीरे–धीरे ये ड्यूटी ही पहचान बन गई। खंडायत और पाइका खानदान खुद को पुश्तैनी रखवाले समझने लगे, जिनकी इज़्ज़त ज़मीन–दान और याद की गई लड़ाइयों से जुड़ी थी।

panels.shot: time-lapse style composite, faded overlays of different rulers’ banners as Paikas remain in the fields
panels.action: The Paika of Odisha stands in the same field as faint ghostly banners of different rulers fade in and out above the horizon, while his posture and the paddy remain constant.

dialogue.text: Dynasties shifted and centres of power moved, from Cuttack to Khurda, yet the land-service link endured. Governments changed, but the old expectation of armed peasants ready to rise lingered on.

i18n.hi: वंश बदलते रहे, सत्ता के ठिकाने कटक से खोरधा तक खिसकते रहे, पर ज़मीन और सेवा की यह डोर टूटती नहीं दिखी। हुकूमतें बदलीं, पर हथियारबंद किसानों के उठ खड़े होने की पुरानी उम्मीद ज्यों की त्यों टिकी रही।

panels.shot: evocative foreshadowing shot, Paika in late-18th-century attire looking towards a distant British-style building
panels.action: In a later time, the Paika of Odisha, now in slightly changed dress, stands on a ridge and looks toward a white-walled building with arched windows and a flag, separated from him by fields and forests.

dialogue.text: Even into the nineteenth century, when new rulers claimed the revenue of Odisha, this old institution flared again in rebellion, as Paikas defended what they saw as their service-earned lands.

i18n.hi: उन्नीसवीं सदी तक भी, जब नए हुक्मरान ओडिशा की लगान पर दावा करने लगे, यही पुरानी संस्था बग़ावत में फिर भड़की, और पाइका उस ज़मीन के लिए लड़े जिसे वे अपनी सेवा की कमाई मानते थे।

panels.shot: quiet, reflective wide shot of the Paika standing between a stone boundary marker and his ploughed field at sunrise
panels.action: At sunrise, the Paika of Odisha stands still between a rough stone boundary marker and his freshly ploughed field, spear grounded beside him as mist curls over the earth.

dialogue.text: The Paika’s rent-free land reminds us how power can be rooted in everyday labour: a kingdom’s defence woven into the lives of its cultivators, where livelihood and duty could never be cleanly separated.

i18n.hi: पाइका की बे-मुज़रिया ज़मीन याद दिलाती है कि ताकत रोज़ की मेहनत में भी जड़ जमा सकती है: जहाँ राज्य की रखवाली खुद किसानों की ज़िंदगी में बुनी हो, और रोज़ी–रोटी और फ़र्ज़ को अलग–अलग करना नामुमकिन हो।

subtitle_i18n.en: Land, Steel and the Drum of the Gajapati
subtitle_i18n.hi: ज़मीन, इस्पात और गजपति का नगाड़ा
